metadata.note: The Atlantic and North Carolina Rail Road ("Old Mullet Road"), Goldsboro - Kinston - Dover - New Bern - Havelock - Morehead City, 96.1 mi (ICC), chartered 1852, built 1855-1858, state majority-owned; and its operating lessees in their own eras. Drawn from research/branches/atlantic_and_north_carolina_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-11-04). Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits by operator, all on identical geometry: A&NC 1857/58-1861 (four opening pieces) and Kinston - Goldsboro to 1865; A&NC 1865-1881; Midland North Carolina Railway (lessee) 1881-1883; A&NC 1883-1904; Howland Improvement Co., trading as the Atlantic & North Carolina Company (lessee) 1904-1906; Norfolk & Southern 1908-1932 (already drawn in norfolk_southern_railway_original.geojson as ns-anc-goldsboro-morehead-city, not changed); A&NC 1939 [ANCHOR]; Atlantic and East Carolina Railway 1939-1950. One A&NC colour across all its eras (the 1877 receivership and 1935 reincorporation are the same company).

not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: New Bern - Dover, Dover - Kinston and New Bern - Morehead City end 1861 as the last CONFIRMED year; service probably ran to the fall of New Bern, 14 Mar 1862, but is unproven.

Kinston - Goldsboro 1862-1863: rests only on the FY 1865 report's "for three years we have run all kind of trains ... from Goldsboro' to Kinston"; passenger receipts are proven for FY 1864-65 only (the 1862-63 and 1863-64 proceedings were not found). STRICT alternative: 1858-1861 plus 1864-1865 as two segments.
1859: no year-specific document read; drawn continuous 1858-1861 on the 1858 report and the FY 1865 statement that the whole road ran passenger trains "for one year before the war".

A&NC 1935-1939: drawn only as a 1939 [ANCHOR]. The Beaufort News (DigitalNC sn91068210) 1935-39 or any 1936-38 Official Guide should settle whether the A&NC ran passenger trains in 1936-38 (DigitalNC was unreachable during research). If confirmed, upgrade to 1936 [OPEN]-1939.

Norfolk Southern rail bus 1935-1937 (blog citing Beaufort News 20 Dec 1934, 3 Jan 1935, NS ad 8 Apr 1937, https://beaufortartist.blogspot.com/2013/01/rail-bus.html): could extend the NS feature to 1935, but 1936-37 conflicts with the A&NC's own operation from late 1935. Nothing drawn on it.
Howland era hand-over to the Norfolk & Southern: Nov 1906 per the NS research; month not read in a primary source.
Midland end: receiver from 19 Mar 1883 (company report) vs 20 Mar (ICC); property returned ~20 May 1883.
The 31 Mar 1950 newspaper pages were seen only as search-engine extracts (DigitalNC refused direct fetches).
headway_min (1440, one train each way a day) is an estimate on every segment; avg_speed_kmh is sourced only for the pre-war pieces (27 mph average, FY 1865 report) and estimated (40) elsewhere.
source_conflicts: Union occupation: ICC valuation via Wikipedia says Federal troops took "part of the line in 1864 and the entire line in 1865"; the A&NC's own FY 1865 report says the larger part had been "in the possession of the United States ... for more than three years" (i.e. since the Mar 1862 capture of New Bern). The company report is preferred.

Passenger end: Carteret County News-Times 31 Mar 1950 ("Last Passenger Train Out Of Morehead City Leaves Today") and its 1958 retrospective vs Wikipedia "would end by 1951" and american-rails "1951" (also "by 1954"). 1950 adopted; the Official Guide's A&EC table dated 30 Apr 1951 is freight and express only.

NS lease end: 1934 "forfeited" (Wikipedia) vs 1935 (default; NS still operating 29 Jul 1935) vs ICC "abandonment" decision 1937 (via Wikipedia) - recorded in the NS layer too; affects only the undrawn 1933-38 gap.
metadata.geometry_check: 2026-11-04: a screenshot review read the Dover - New Bern piece as a ruled straight line ~2 mi north of the railway. Checked and NOT a defect: the line was re-traced from OSM (same 91.6 mi, same alignment); the 55 raw OSM nodes of the EC Line between Dover and New Bern lie within 4 m of the drawn line, Cove City and Tuscarora geocode 0.0 km from it, and the only other rail within 8 km is the NS NB-Line to the north and abandoned ACL grade to the south. The basemap line passing south of Cove City is US 70, not the railway. The A&NC is straight across this stretch. The NS layer's ns-anc-goldsboro-morehead-city geometry (54 vertices, DP 8 m) is the same alignment and was left unchanged; this layer now uses its own 5 m re-trace (73 vertices).

segments.note: Opening section. From 1 Jan 1857 a second-class passenger car ran with the construction train New Bern - Core Creek (today's Cove), connecting with the New Bern - Kinston - Goldsboro stage line; extended to Rouse's (= Dover, 24 mi) 3 Apr 1857 and to Tilghman's (27 mi, a few miles past Dover) 28 May 1857. Mixed-train passenger service, steam from the outset. Through service from 1858 (see the other pre-war pieces); the company "for one year before the war ... operated the whole Road" with passenger trains. This end is [OPEN]: 1861 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - service probably ran until New Bern fell on 14 Mar 1862, but no source dates it. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day), not sourced.

segments.note: Trains reached Moseley Hall (La Grange) 17 Feb 1858 and "On the 20th day of April, the Road was opened to Goldsboro'" (1858 report). The only part of the road the company kept through the Civil War (Confederate side of the lines after New Bern fell, Mar 1862). FY June 1864 - Mar 1865 shows $32,519 "Passenger" and $20,220 "Way Travel" receipts on these 26 miles, separate from troop and government transport, so this is genuine passenger service; the same report says "for three years we have run all kind of trains ... from Goldsboro' to Kinston". Ends Mar 1865, when the US Army took it ("since the middle of March last"); the Army ran it as part of the Military Railroad Raleigh - Morehead City until 26 Oct 1865 (military operation, not drawn). 1862-63 rest only on the "all kind of trains ... for three years" statement: the STRICT alternative is 1858-1861 plus 1864-1865 (see metadata.not_yet_sourced). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day), not sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] - one year only. After the Norfolk Southern lease ended (A&NC voted 8 Aug 1935 not to re-lease; reincorporated 16 Nov 1935) the state-owned A&NC ran the line itself until leasing it to the Atlantic and East Carolina from 1 Aug 1939. Only the 1939 handover is supported, by Wikipedia's statement that passenger trains passed "from the Atlantic and North Carolina name to the Atlantic and East Carolina" name. A&NC passenger service in 1935-38 is very likely (a 1936 Beaufort News mention of "the Atlantic and North Carolina train" for the Sunday mail; conductor J. B. Davis, fired after the 1939 takeover for not collecting fares) but no source read proves passengers. Service certainly ran wider both ways; do not widen this anchor without a 1935-38 Guide or newspaper showing an A&NC passenger train. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day), not sourced.

segments.note: Lessee era (Rule 4 split, identical geometry). Leased 1 Sep 1904 "for 91 years and 4 months" to the Howland Improvement Co. (R. S. Howland, Asheville), which operated it as "the Atlantic & North Carolina Company" (FY 1906 report) - a lessee corporation distinct from the lessor Atlantic and North Carolina Rail Road Co. The company string is "Howland Improvement Company" deliberately, so that Rule 4's name normalisation does not merge the lessee with the lessor; the label carries the trading name. The lessee bought six new passenger coaches (FY 1905) and built new passenger depots at Kinston, Morehead City and Dover (FY 1906); Fowler 1905G (Mansfield) and 1906G (Neuse Crossing). Absorbed into the Norfolk & Southern consolidation, Nov 1906 (per the NS research; exact month not read in a primary source); by FY to Aug 1907 the road was "operated and known as the Norfolk & Southern Railway". 1904 is the lease date on an uninterrupted service. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day), not sourced.

segments.note: Atlantic and East Carolina Railway (chartered 19 Jun 1939; lease effective 1 Aug 1939; HQ Kinston), passenger trains continuing across the change from the A&NC. One train a day each way, Goldsboro Union Station - Morehead City, timed to connect at Goldsboro with a Southern overnight train (Wikipedia, citing the Jan 1950 Official Guide). Wartime traffic heavy (Camp Lejeune, Cherry Point MCAS); Cherry Point station in the 1947 Guide and Piney Grove / Edgewater in the 1949 working timetable (Fowler). The railroad petitioned to drop the train in June 1949; the last passenger train left Morehead City at 4 p.m. on 31 Mar 1950 (Carteret County News-Times). Freight and express only thereafter (Guide table dated 30 Apr 1951) - not drawn; Southern Railway stock control 1957 came after passengers had gone. CONFLICT: Wikipedia ("would end by 1951") and american-rails ("1951") vs the contemporary 1950 headline - the newspaper is preferred and the 1951 Guide agrees. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day), not sourced.
